## Loading packages

To use Psy to calculate confidence intervals over contrast effects, we will use a workflow that uses functions from [afex](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/afex/versions/1.4-1) to implement ANOVA models, and [emmeans](https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/) to obtain estimated marginal means and the required contrast estimates. So let's load those packages, and any others that are helpful for our workflow.

```{r, loadpackages}

library(afex)
library(emmeans)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(PsyR)

```

## The data

Lets load the data, then call the `head()` function to print the first 5 rows.

```{r loaddata}

data(fatigue)
head(fatigue, 5)
```

Have you forgotten the details of the fatigue dataset? Call the help function using `?data` to open its documentation.

```{r, whatfatigue}

?fatigue
```

Time for some tidying! `mutate()` creates a new column called "Group", then assigns the labels of "Alert", "Mild", "Moderate" and "Extreme" to the previously coded group levels 1 2 3 4. We have also called the `factor()` function, assigning our new column as a factor rather than a double. This will be helpful later when we visualise our data, not to mention that it makes for some more human readable category names!
```{r sortfatigue}

fatigue <- fatigue %>%
             mutate(Group = factor(Group, 
                                  levels=c(1,2,3,4),
                                  labels=c('Alert', 
                                           'Mild', 
                                          'Moderate',
                                          'Extreme')))
```

Time to plot our data, with help from the ggplot2 package.  
First, using a pipe, lets tell `ggplot()` to use the fatigue dataset (the one we just edited, with the better labels :grin:). Then, within `aes()` lets create a canvas with "Group" on the X axis and "Errors" on the Y axis. Lets also fill our boxplots based on the Group they represent. 

Next, lets create a boxplot `geom_boxplot()` and make it look nice and clean using `theme_classic()`.

```{r boxplotit}

fatigue %>% ggplot(aes(x = Group, y = Errors, fill = Group)) +
  geom_boxplot() + theme_classic()

```

Lets run some statistical tests! First, lets specify that we want a multivariate analysis, using the `afex_options()` function. Next, lets create a new object *mod*, 

```{r, aov}

# set emmeans option to multivariate
afex_options(emmeans_model = "multivariate")
# perform the statistical model
mod <- aov_ez("id", 
              "Errors", 
              fatigue, 
              between = "Group")

emms <- emmeans(mod, "Group")
emms

```
```{r definecontrasts}
### note to selves - is there a way to get emmeans to do the scaling here?

between_contrasts = list(
  "Fatigue-Alert" = c(-1, 1/3, 1/3, 1/3),
  "Extreme-Mod,Mild" = c(0, -1/2, -1/2, 1),
  "Low-Hi" = c(1/2, 1/2, -1/2, -1/2),
  "Alert-Mild" = c(1, -1, 0, 0)
)
between_contrasts
```

```{r, between_fx}

btwn_fx <- contrast(emms, between_contrasts)
btwn_fx
```

```{r, psyci}


contrasts_w_cis = psyci(mod, contrast_tables=list(btwn_fx),  family_list=list("b"), method="ph", alpha=.05, between_factors = list("Group"))

```
